key_insight: The paper argues that ensuring AI is legible, steerable, and cooperative with humans will require new mathematics across several core fields, not just incremental model improvements.
engineering_relevance: For AI safety systems, the most relevant math areas are logic/game theory for cooperation, probability for agency and world-models, algebra for learned features, and analysis/geometry for generalization and training dynamics.
method: Organizes the topic by mathematical field so readers can enter through their own expertise.
Connects each field to a specific AI safety target: cooperation, world-modeling, feature structure, and training behavior.
Ends each section with an open problem aimed at mathematicians without prior AI safety background.
evidence_signal: The abstract is a conceptual invitation rather than an empirical study, so it provides no data, benchmarks, or quantitative evaluation.
watch_item: The proposals are broad and foundational, so translating them into concrete safety methods may be difficult without a clear empirical validation path.
paper_title: Math for AI safety: an invitation for mathematicians
